ordinary.title: Ordinary form
ordinary.intro: The Mass as it is celebrated in most parishes, from the Roman Missal as revised after the Second Vatican Council (third edition, 2002; this English translation since 2011). It has two great parts, the Liturgy of the Word and the Liturgy of the Eucharist, with short rites to open and to close.
notes: Postures are those of the dioceses of the United States. If the people around you do otherwise, do as they do.

The short responses are given in full. The longer prayers said together are given by their first words, with the Latin and an older English translation to read: the words now used at Mass in English are under copyright and are not carried here. They are in the missalette in the pew.

parts.title: Introductory Rites
parts.about: We gather as one people, ask God’s mercy and are made ready to listen.

sections.title: Entrance
sections.about: The priest and ministers come to the altar, usually while a hymn or the entrance antiphon is sung. The priest kisses the altar, which stands for Christ.

sections.title: Sign of the Cross and greeting
sections.about: All make the sign of the cross with the priest. His greeting and our answer are a prayer for one another.

lines.cue: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
The Lord be with you.
lines.note: Or a longer greeting. A bishop says “Peace be with you.”

sections.title: Penitential Act
sections.about: A short silence to call our sins to mind, then one of three forms. Often it is the Confiteor, said by all together.

lines.cue: I confess to almighty God…
lines.note: Strike your breast at the words “through my fault”, said three times.
lines.prayerNote: The older, longer form. The form said at Mass now is shorter and is addressed also to “you, my brothers and sisters”.

lines.r: Or the priest says two short verses, and the people answer each:

lines.say: For we have sinned against you.

lines.r: Or three invocations of Christ, each ending “Lord, have mercy” or “Christ, have mercy”, which the people repeat.
Then the priest asks God to have mercy on us and forgive us:

sections.title: Lord, have mercy
sections.about: Said or sung unless it was already part of the Penitential Act. Each line is answered with the same words. It may be sung in Greek: the Roman Mass took it from the East about the fifth century.

sections.title: Glory to God
sections.about: The song of the angels at Bethlehem, grown into a hymn of praise to the Father and the Son. It is sung or said by all.

lines.cue: Glory to God in the highest…

sections.when: On Sundays outside Advent and Lent, on solemnities and feasts, and in the octaves of Christmas and Easter.

sections.title: Collect
sections.about: The priest says “Let us pray”, and there is a silence in which each brings his own needs. He then gathers them into one prayer, which belongs to the day.

parts.title: Liturgy of the Word
parts.about: God speaks to his people in the Scriptures, and we answer in the psalm, the Creed and our prayers.

sections.title: First Reading
sections.about: On Sundays it is usually from the Old Testament and chosen to go with the Gospel; in Easter time it is from the Acts of the Apostles. On weekdays it may be from either Testament.

lines.cue: The word of the Lord.

sections.title: Responsorial Psalm
sections.about: A psalm answering the reading. The cantor or reader gives a short response; all repeat it, and again after each verse.

sections.title: Second Reading
sections.about: From the letters of the Apostles or the Apocalypse.

lines.cue: The word of the Lord.

sections.title: Gospel Acclamation
sections.about: All stand to greet Christ, who speaks in the Gospel. The Alleluia is sung with a verse; in Lent another short acclamation of praise takes its place.

sections.title: Gospel
sections.about: Read by a deacon or the priest. As the Gospel is announced, trace a small cross with the thumb on your forehead, lips and breast: may his word be in my mind, on my lips and in my heart.

lines.cue: The Lord be with you.
A reading from the holy Gospel according to…

lines.r: The Gospel is read. At the end:

lines.cue: The Gospel of the Lord.

lines.say: Praise to you, Lord Jesus Christ.

sections.title: Homily
sections.about: The priest or deacon opens up the readings and applies them to life. A short silence often follows.

sections.title: Profession of Faith
sections.about: All profess the faith of the Church in the Nicene Creed. Bow at the words that tell of the Incarnation, from “and by the Holy Spirit” to “and became man”; at Christmas and on the Annunciation, genuflect instead. The shorter Apostles’ Creed may be used, especially in Lent and Easter time.

lines.cue: I believe in one God…

lines.r: Or the Apostles’ Creed:

lines.cue: I believe in God, the Father almighty…

sections.title: Universal Prayer
sections.about: Also called the Prayer of the Faithful. We pray for the Church, for the world and those who govern, for those in need and for our own community, and often for the dead. After each intention all answer; the response varies, but is usually this one.

parts.title: Liturgy of the Eucharist
parts.about: What Christ did at the Last Supper is done again: bread and wine are brought, the great prayer of thanksgiving is said over them, and they become his Body and Blood, his sacrifice made present.

sections.title: Preparation of the Gifts
sections.about: The altar is prepared and the bread and wine are brought up, often with the collection. This is the moment to place your own day and your intentions on the altar with them. If there is no singing, the priest may say the two prayers of blessing aloud, and all answer each.

sections.title: Pray, brethren
sections.about: The priest asks all to pray that the sacrifice, his and ours, may be acceptable to God. Stand as he says this.

lines.cue: Pray, brethren…
May the Lord accept the sacrifice at your hands…

sections.title: Prayer over the Offerings
sections.about: A short prayer of the day over the bread and wine.

sections.title: Preface dialogue
sections.about: The Eucharistic Prayer, the centre of the whole Mass, opens with this exchange. The priest then gives thanks to the Father in the Preface, which changes with the season and the feast.

lines.cue: The Lord be with you.
Lift up your hearts.

lines.say: We lift them up to the Lord.

lines.cue: Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.

sections.title: Holy, Holy, Holy
sections.about: We join the song of the angels that Isaiah heard, and the cry of the crowds on Palm Sunday. Sung or said by all.

lines.cue: Holy, Holy, Holy Lord God of hosts…

sections.title: Eucharistic Prayer
sections.about: Kneel when the Sanctus ends. The priest alone says the prayer, in the name of all. He calls down the Holy Spirit on the gifts, holding his hands over them, and repeats the words of Christ at the Last Supper: at these words the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ. He raises the Host, and then the Chalice, for all to see; a bell may be rung. Look up and adore. Many say silently “My Lord and my God.”

sections.title: The Mystery of Faith
sections.about: After the consecration the priest says “The mystery of faith”, and all answer with one of three acclamations, usually sung. They begin:

lines.cue: We proclaim your Death, O Lord…
When we eat this Bread and drink this Cup…
Save us, Savior of the world…

sections.title: Doxology and Great Amen
sections.about: The prayer goes on to remember Christ’s death and rising, to offer his sacrifice to the Father and to pray for the Church, the living and the dead. It ends as the priest lifts up the Host and the Chalice: “Through him, and with him, and in him…”. Our Amen makes the whole prayer our own. It is often sung.

parts.title: Communion Rite
parts.about: The last part of the Liturgy of the Eucharist. We prepare, as one family, to receive the Lord.

sections.title: The Lord’s Prayer
sections.about: All say or sing the prayer Jesus taught. The priest alone continues, asking for deliverance from every evil, and all conclude.

lines.cue: Our Father, who art in heaven…

lines.r: After the priest’s prayer, “Deliver us, Lord…”:

lines.say: For the kingdom, the power and the glory are yours now and for ever.

sections.title: Sign of Peace
sections.about: The priest prays for the peace and unity of the Church, and all answer. He may then invite all to offer a sign of peace to those nearby: a handshake or a bow, with the words “Peace be with you.”

lines.r: At the end of the priest’s prayer for peace:

lines.cue: The peace of the Lord be with you always.

sections.title: Lamb of God
sections.about: Sung or said while the priest breaks the Host, as Christ broke the bread.

lines.say: Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.
Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world, grant us peace.

sections.title: Behold the Lamb of God
sections.about: Kneel after the Lamb of God, unless your bishop has decided otherwise. The priest shows the Host and says “Behold the Lamb of God…”. All answer in the words of the centurion who asked Jesus to heal his servant.

lines.cue: Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof…
lines.prayerNote: The older English. The words said now are the same but for “you” in place of “thou”.

sections.title: Holy Communion
sections.about: Catholics who are not conscious of grave sin, and who have fasted from food and drink for an hour before Communion (water and medicine excepted), may receive. Go up when your row does. In the United States Communion is received standing, though you may kneel. Bow your head as you come before the minister, and answer “Amen”; receive on the tongue or in the hand, and consume the Host at once. If you are not receiving, stay in your place and make an act of spiritual communion. In many parishes those not receiving may come forward with arms crossed for a blessing; that is a local custom, not part of the rite.

lines.cue: The Body of Christ.

lines.r: Where the Chalice is offered: “The Blood of Christ.” “Amen.”
An act of spiritual communion:

sections.title: Silence after Communion
sections.about: Kneel or sit, and speak to the Lord whom you have received. A hymn or psalm of praise may be sung.

sections.title: Prayer after Communion
sections.about: The priest says “Let us pray” and asks that what we have received may bear fruit in us.

parts.title: Concluding Rites
parts.about: We are blessed and sent out to live what we have celebrated.

sections.title: Blessing
sections.about: Any brief announcements come first. Make the sign of the cross as the priest blesses you. On some days the blessing is longer, with an Amen after each part.

lines.cue: The Lord be with you.
May almighty God bless you, the Father, and the Son, ✠ and the Holy Spirit.

sections.title: Dismissal
sections.about: The word “Mass” comes from this sending: Ite, missa est. The priest kisses the altar and leaves with the ministers, usually during a hymn. Many stay a moment to give thanks.

lines.cue: Go forth, the Mass is ended.

traditional.title: Traditional Latin Mass
traditional.intro: The Mass according to the Roman Missal of 1962, also called the extraordinary form or the Tridentine Mass. It is said in Latin, the priest facing the altar with the people, and much of it is prayed quietly. It has two parts: the Mass of the Catechumens, which teaches, and the Mass of the Faithful, the sacrifice itself.
notes: You do not have to keep up with every word. The older custom is simply to unite yourself with what the priest is doing: follow the outline here, read a prayer or two, and look up at the altar. The bell marks the moments that matter most.

At a Low Mass the server answers the priest. Where the people answer too (a “dialogue Mass”), they say the server’s lines. At a sung Mass the choir, and often the people, sing the responses and the Kyrie, Gloria, Credo, Sanctus and Agnus Dei.

The Church gives no rule for the people’s postures at this Mass, and customs vary from place to place. Those shown are common in the United States; where two customs are both common, one had to be chosen. Do as the people around you do.

The prayers that change with the day (the Introit, Collect, Epistle, Gradual, Gospel, Offertory, Secret, Preface, Communion and Postcommunion) are not in the app. A hand missal or the parish leaflet has them.

A Mass for the dead (a Requiem) differs in a few places: Psalm 42 at the start, the Gloria Patri and the final blessing are omitted, and the Agnus Dei ends “dona eis requiem”, grant them rest. Psalm 42 is also omitted from Passion Sunday until Easter. What is proper to a solemn Mass with deacon and subdeacon is left out here.
traditional.credit: Latin text and English translation of the Order of Mass from the Divinum Officium project, used under the MIT licence, with a few slips in the English corrected. The explanations between the prayers are in part theirs and in part written for Biblica.

parts.title: Mass of the Catechumens
parts.about: Prayer, praise and instruction. In the early Church those preparing for baptism stayed for this part and left before the sacrifice.

sections.title: Asperges
sections.about: The priest sprinkles the altar and then the people with holy water, a reminder of baptism, while the antiphon is sung. Make the sign of the cross as you are sprinkled. In Easter time the antiphon is “Vidi aquam” instead.

lines.la: Aspérges me, Dómine, hyssópo, et mundábor: lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
lines.en: Thou shalt sprinkle me, O Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; Thou shalt wash me, and I shall become whiter than snow.

lines.la: Miserére mei, Deus, secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
lines.en: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy.

lines.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

lines.la: Aspérges me, Dómine, hyssópo, et mundábor: lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
lines.en: Thou shalt sprinkle me, O Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; Thou shalt wash me, and I shall become whiter than snow.

lines.la: Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam.
lines.en: Show us, O Lord, Thy mercy.

lines.la: Et salutáre tuum da nobis.
lines.en: And grant us Thy salvation.

lines.la: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
lines.en: O Lord, hear my prayer.

lines.la: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
lines.en: And let my cry come before Thee.

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.la: Orémus.
lines.en: Let us pray.

lines.la: Exáudi nos, Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus, et míttere dignéris sanctum Angelum tuum de cælis, qui custódiat, fóveat, prótegat, vísitet atque deféndat omnes habitántes in hoc habitáculo. Per Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: Hear us, O holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, and vouchsafe to send Thy holy Angel from heaven, to guard, cherish, protect, visit and defend all that are assembled in this place: through Christ our Lord. Amen.

sections.when: Before the principal sung Mass on Sundays.

sections.title: Prayers at the foot of the altar
sections.about: Stand as the priest comes in. He and the server prepare to go up to the altar: Psalm 42, and the Confiteor, first his and then ours. At a sung Mass the choir sings the Introit meanwhile.

lines.r: The priest, bowing down at the foot of the altar, makes the Sign of the Cross, from his forehead to his breast, and says:

lines.la: In nómine Patris, ✠ et Fílii, et Spíritus Sancti. Amen.
lines.en: In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, ✠ and of the Holy Ghost. Amen.

lines.r: Then joining his hands before his breast, he begins the Anthem:

lines.la: Introíbo ad altáre Dei.
lines.en: I will go in to the altar of God.

lines.la: Ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
lines.en: To God who giveth joy to my youth.

lines.r: The priest alternates with the server in reciting this psalm to express his desire, joy and confidence in going to the altar of the Sacrifice.

lines.la: Júdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso érue me.
lines.en: Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation which is not holy: deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

lines.la: Quia tu es, Deus, fortitúdo mea: quare me repulísti, et quare tristis incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
lines.en: For Thou, O God, art my strength: why hast Thou cast me off? and why go I sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?

lines.la: Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum et in tabernácula tua.
lines.en: Send forth Thy light and Thy truth: they have conducted me and brought me unto Thy holy mount, and into Thy tabernacles.

lines.la: Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
lines.en: And I will go in to the altar of God: to God who giveth joy to my youth.

lines.la: Confitébor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: quare tristis es, ánima mea, et quare contúrbas me?
lines.en: To Thee, O God, my God, I will give praise upon the harp; why art thou sad, O my soul, and why dost thou disquiet me?

lines.la: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
lines.en: Hope in God, for I will still give praise to Him: the salvation of my countenance and my God.

lines.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
lines.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.

lines.la: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper: et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

lines.r: The priest repeats the Anthem:

lines.la: Introíbo ad altáre Dei.
lines.en: I will go in to the altar of God.

lines.la: Ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
lines.en: To God who giveth joy to my youth.

lines.r: The priest, signing himself with the Sign of the Cross, says:

lines.la: Adjutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.
lines.en: Our help ✠ is in the Name of the Lord.

lines.la: Qui fecit cælum et terram.
lines.en: Who made heaven and earth.

lines.r: Then, joining his hands, and humbly bowing down, he says the Confiteor:

lines.la: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Joánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, ómnibus Sanctis, et vobis, fratres: quia peccávi nimis cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ideo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Joánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, omnes Sanctos, et vos, fratres, oráre pro me ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.
lines.en: I confess to almighty God, to the blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the Saints, and to you, brothers, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word, and deed, (Here he strikes his breast thrice.) through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech the blessed Mary, ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, all the Saints, and you, brothers, to pray to the Lord our God for me.

lines.la: Misereátur tui omnípotens Deus, et, dimíssis peccátis tuis, perdúcat te ad vitam ætérnam.
lines.en: May almighty God be merciful to thee, and forgiving thy sins, bring thee to everlasting life.

lines.r: The priest answers:

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: The server says the Confiteor.

lines.la: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Joánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, ómnibus Sanctis, et tibi, pater: quia peccávi nimis cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ideo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Joánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, omnes Sanctos, et te, pater, oráre pro me ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.
lines.en: I confess to almighty God, to the blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the Saints, and to you, Father, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word, and deed, through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech the blessed Mary, ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, all the Saints, and you, Father, to pray to the Lord our God for me.

lines.r: Then the priest, with his hands joined, says:

lines.la: Misereátur vestri omnípotens Deus, et, dimíssis peccátis vestris, perdúcat vos ad vitam ætérnam.
lines.en: May almighty God be merciful to you, and forgiving your sins, bring you to everlasting life.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: Signing himself with the Sign of the Cross, the priest says:

lines.la: Indulgéntiam, ✠ absolutiónem et remissiónem peccatórum nostrórum tríbuat nobis omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
lines.en: May the ✠ almighty and merciful Lord grant us pardon, absolution, and remission of our sins.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: Bowing down, he proceeds:

lines.la: Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos.
lines.en: O God, Thou wilt turn again and quicken us.

lines.la: Et plebs tua lætábitur in te.
lines.en: And thy people shall rejoice in Thee.

lines.la: Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam.
lines.en: Show us, O Lord, Thy mercy.

lines.la: Et salutáre tuum da nobis.
lines.en: And grant us Thy salvation.

lines.la: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
lines.en: O Lord, hear my prayer.

lines.la: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
lines.en: And let my cry come before Thee.

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.r: First extending, then joining his hands, the priest says audibly: "Let us pray". Then ascending to the altar, he says secretly:

lines.la: Orémus.
lines.en: Let us pray.

lines.la: Aufer a nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, iniquitátes nostras: ut ad Sancta sanctórum puris mereámur méntibus introíre. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: Take away from us our iniquities, we beseech Thee, O Lord, that we may be worthy to enter with pure minds into the Holy of Holies, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.r: His hands joined, and bowing down over the altar, the priest says:

lines.la: Orámus te, Dómine, per mérita Sanctórum tuórum, quorum relíquiæ hic sunt, et ómnium Sanctórum: ut indulgére dignéris ómnia peccáta mea. Amen.
lines.en: We beseech Thee, O Lord, by the merits of Thy Saints, (He kisses the sacred stone) whose relics are here, and of all the Saints, that Thou wouldst vouchsafe to forgive me all my sins. Amen.

sections.note: Psalm 42 is omitted at Masses for the dead and from Passion Sunday until Easter.

sections.title: Incensing of the altar
sections.about: At a sung Mass the priest blesses incense and incenses the altar before he reads the Introit.

lines.r: At a sung or solemn Mass the altar is incensed here. The server (at a solemn Mass, the deacon) says:

lines.la: Benedícite, pater reverénde
lines.en: Bless, reverend father!

lines.r: Whilst blessing the incense the priest says:

lines.la: Ab illo bene ✠ dicáris, in cujus honóre cremáberis. Amen.
lines.en: Be blessed ✠ by Him in whose honor thou art burnt. Amen.

sections.title: Introit
sections.about: The entrance verse of the day, read by the priest at the right-hand side of the altar. It gives the Mass its name: Requiem, Gaudete, Laetare.

lines.x: The Introit of the day is read here.

sections.title: Kyrie
sections.about: Nine cries for mercy in Greek, three to each Person of the Trinity. Priest and server take them in turn.

lines.la: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.en: Lord, have mercy.

lines.la: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.en: Lord, have mercy.

lines.la: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.en: Lord, have mercy.

lines.la: Christe, eléison.
lines.en: Christ, have mercy.

lines.la: Christe, eléison.
lines.en: Christ, have mercy.

lines.la: Christe, eléison.
lines.en: Christ, have mercy.

lines.la: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.en: Lord, have mercy.

lines.la: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.en: Lord, have mercy.

lines.la: Kýrie, eléison.
lines.en: Lord, have mercy.

sections.title: Gloria
sections.about: The hymn of the angels. At a sung Mass, sit when the priest sits while the choir finishes it.

lines.r: Afterwards, standing at the middle of the altar, extending and then joining his hands, and bowing slightly, the priest says — except during Lent, Advent and in Masses for the Dead — the Gloria. When he says the words: We adore Thee, We give Thee thanks; Jesus Christ; and Receive our prayer, he bows, and at the end he signs himself with the Sign of the Cross from forehead to breast:

lines.la: Glória in excélsis Deo. Et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis. Laudámus te. Benedícimus te. Adorámus te. Glorificámus te. Grátias ágimus tibi propter magnam glóriam tuam. Dómine Deus, Rex cæléstis, Deus Pater omnípotens. Dómine Fili unigénite, Jesu Christe. Dómine Deus, Agnus Dei, Fílius Patris. Qui tollis peccáta mundi, miserére nobis. Qui tollis peccáta mundi, súscipe deprecatiónem nostram. Qui sedes ad déxteram Patris, miserére nobis. Quóniam tu solus Sanctus. Tu solus Dóminus. Tu solus Altíssimus, Jesu Christe. Cum Sancto Spíritu ✠ in glória Dei Patris. Amen.
lines.en: Glory be to God on high, and on earth peace to men of good will. We praise Thee. We bless Thee. We adore Thee. We glorify Thee. We give Thee thanks for Thy great glory. O Lord God, heavenly King, God the Father almighty. O Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son. O Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father. Who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. Who takest away the sins of the world, receive our prayer. Who sittest at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us. For Thou only art holy. Thou only art the Lord. Thou only art most high, O Jesus Christ. Together with the Holy Ghost ✠ in the glory of God the Father. Amen.

sections.when: On feasts, and on Sundays outside Advent, Septuagesima and Lent. Not at Masses for the dead.

sections.title: Collect
sections.about: The priest kisses the altar, greets the people and sings or says the prayer of the day. There may be more than one.

lines.r: Then the priest kisses the altar, and turning to the people says:

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.r: The Collects mean the collected prayers of all the faithful assisting at the Holy Sacrifice. Raising his voice, his hands, and his sentiments to God, the priest excites the faithful to unite their prayers with his.

lines.x: The Collect of the day is said here. The server answers “Amen.”

sections.title: Epistle
sections.about: A reading, most often from the letters of Saint Paul, read in Latin at the altar. At the end the server answers “Deo gratias”, thanks be to God. It is commonly read again in English before the sermon.

lines.x: The Epistle of the day is read here. At the end the server answers “Deo gratias.”

lines.la: Deo grátias.
lines.en: Thanks be to God.

sections.title: Gradual and Alleluia
sections.about: Verses of the psalms between the readings. From Septuagesima to Easter a Tract replaces the Alleluia; on a few great feasts a Sequence is added.

lines.x: The Gradual and Alleluia (or Tract) of the day are read here.

sections.title: Gospel
sections.about: The missal is carried to the left-hand side of the altar and all stand. As the priest announces the Gospel, sign your forehead, lips and breast with the thumb. The server answers at the beginning and at the end.

lines.r: The Missal is transferred to the other side of the altar. At Low Masses, the priest, bowing down at the middle of the altar, with his hands joined, says:

lines.la: Munda cor meum ac lábia mea, omnípotens Deus, qui lábia Isaíæ Prophétæ cálculo mundásti igníto: ita me tua grata miseratióne dignáre mundáre, ut sanctum Evangélium tuum digne váleam nuntiáre. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: Cleanse my heart and my lips, O almighty God, who didst cleanse the lips of the prophet Isaias with a burning coal, and vouchsafe, through Thy gracious mercy, so to purify me, that I may worthily announce Thy holy Gospel. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.la: Jube, Dómine, benedícere. Dóminus sit in corde meo et in lábiis meis: ut digne et competénter annúntiem Evangélium suum. Amen.
lines.en: Give me Thy blessing, O Lord. The Lord be in my heart and on my lips, that I may worthily and in a becoming manner, proclaim His holy Gospel. Amen.

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.r: The priest announces the Gospel: “Sequentia (or Initium) sancti Evangelii secundum…”

lines.la: Glória tibi, Dómine.
lines.en: Glory be to Thee, O Lord.

lines.x: The Gospel of the day is read here.

lines.la: Laus tibi, Christe.
lines.en: Praise be to Thee, O Christ.

lines.la: Per Evangélica dicta, deleántur nostra delícta.
lines.en: By the words of the Gospel may our sins be blotted out.

sections.title: Sermon
sections.about: The Epistle and Gospel are usually read in English first (stand for the Gospel), followed by the announcements and the sermon.
sections.when: On Sundays and holy days; often omitted on weekdays.

sections.title: Credo
sections.about: The Nicene Creed. Genuflect with the priest at “Et incarnatus est… et homo factus est”. At a sung Mass, kneel at those words when the choir sings them, and sit when the priest sits.

lines.r: On Sundays and certain Feasts the priest recites the Creed, a summary of the Catholic Doctrine. This profession of faith was drawn up in the General Councils of Nicaea in 325 and Constantinople in 381 to condemn heretics who denied that Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost were God.

lines.la: Credo in unum Deum, Patrem omnipoténtem, factórem cæli et terræ, visibílium ómnium et invisibílium. Et in unum Dóminum Jesum Christum, Fílium Dei unigénitum. Et ex Patre natum ante ómnia sǽcula. Deum de Deo, Lumen de Lúmine, Deum verum de Deo vero. Génitum, non factum, consubstantiálem Patri: per quem ómnia facta sunt. Qui propter nos hómines et propter nostram salútem descéndit de cælis. Et incarnátus est de Spíritu Sancto ex María Vírgine: Et homo factus est. Crucifíxus étiam pro nobis: sub Póntio Piláto passus, et sepúltus est. Et resurréxit tértia die, secúndum Scriptúras. Et ascéndit in cælum: sedet ad déxteram Patris. Et íterum ventúrus est cum glória judicáre vivos et mórtuos: cujus regni non erit finis. Et in Spíritum Sanctum, Dóminum et vivificántem: qui ex Patre Filióque procédit. Qui cum Patre et Fílio simul adorátur et conglorificátur: qui locútus est per Prophétas. Et unam sanctam cathólicam et apostólicam Ecclésiam. Confíteor unum baptísma in remissiónem peccatórum. Et exspécto resurrectiónem mortuórum. Et vitam ventúri sæculi. Amen.
lines.en: I believe in one God, the Father almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things, visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God. And born of the Father, before all ages. God of God: Light of Light: true God of true God. Begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father, by whom all things were made. Who, for us men, and for our salvation, came down from heaven. (Here kneel down.) And became incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary: and was made man. He was crucified also for us, suffered under Pontius Pilate, and was buried. And the third day He rose again according to the Scriptures. And ascended into heaven, and sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And He shall come again with glory to judge both the living and the dead, of whose kingdom there shall be no end. And in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of Life, proceeding from the Father and the Son. Who together, with the Father and the Son, is adored and glorified: Who spoke by the prophets. And in one, holy, Catholic and Apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. And I look for the resurrection of the dead. And the life of the world to come. Amen.

sections.when: On Sundays and the greater feasts.

parts.title: Mass of the Faithful
parts.about: The sacrifice: the offering, the consecration and Communion.

sections.title: Offertory
sections.about: The priest offers the bread and then the wine, into which he has put a drop of water. The prayers are said quietly; a bell may be rung as he uncovers the chalice. Offer yourself and your intentions with the gifts.

lines.r: The priest kisses the altar, and turning to the people says:

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.r: After saluting the people once more, the priest enters upon the Sacrifice of the Mass proper and urges the faithful to pray with him.

lines.la: Orémus.
lines.en: Let us pray.

lines.x: The Offertory verse of the day is read here.

lines.r: Then the priest reads the Offertory-verse, a short quotation from Holy Scripture which varies with the Mass of each day. This being finished, he offers the bread and wine, which, by virtue of the words of consecration, he is going to change into the adorable Body and Blood of Jesus Christ. He takes the paten with the host and offering it up, says:

lines.la: Súscipe, sancte Pater, omnípotens ætérne Deus, hanc immaculátam hóstiam, quam ego indígnus fámulus tuus óffero tibi Deo meo vivo et vero, pro innumerabílibus peccátis, et offensiónibus, et neglegéntiis meis, et pro ómnibus circumstántibus, sed et pro ómnibus fidélibus christiánis vivis atque defúnctis: ut mihi, et illis profíciat ad salútem in vitam ætérnam. Amen.
lines.en: Accept, O holy Father, almighty and eternal God, this unspotted host, which I, Thy unworthy servant, offer unto Thee, my living and true God, for my innumerable sins, offenses, and negligences, and for all here present: as also for all faithful Christians, both living and dead, that it may avail both me and them for salvation unto life everlasting. Amen.

lines.r: Making the Sign of the Cross with the paten, he places the host upon the corporal. He pours wine and water into the chalice, blessing the water before it is mixed. He pours a few drops of water into the chalice containing wine, in remembrance of the water and blood which flowed from the side of Jesus when pierced by the soldier's lance.

lines.la: Deus, ✠ qui humánæ substántiæ dignitátem mirabíliter condidísti, et mirabílius reformásti: da nobis per hujus aquæ et vini mystérium, ejus divinitátis esse consórtes, qui humanitátis nostræ fíeri dignátus est párticeps, Jesus Christus, Fílius tuus, Dóminus noster: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus: per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: O God, who, in creating human nature, didst wonderfully dignify it, and still more wonderfully restore it, grant that, by the Mystery of this water and wine, we may be made partakers of His divine nature, who vouchsafed to be made partaker of our human nature, even Jesus Christ our Lord, Thy Son, who with Thee, liveth and reigneth in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God: world without end. Amen.

lines.r: Then the priest takes the chalice, and offers it, saying:

lines.la: Offérimus tibi, Dómine, cálicem salutáris, tuam deprecántes cleméntiam: ut in conspéctu divínæ majestátis tuæ, pro nostra et totíus mundi salúte, cum odóre suavitátis ascéndat. Amen.
lines.en: We offer unto Thee, O Lord, the chalice of salvation, beseeching Thy clemency, that it may ascend before Thy divine Majesty, as a sweet savor, for our salvation, and for that of the whole world. Amen.

lines.r: The priest makes the Sign of the Cross with the chalice, places it upon the corporal, and covers it with the pall. Then, with his hands joined upon the Altar, and slightly bowing down, he says:

lines.la: In spíritu humilitátis et in ánimo contríto suscipiámur a te, Dómine: et sic fiat sacrifícium nostrum in conspéctu tuo hódie, ut pláceat tibi, Dómine Deus.
lines.en: Accept us, O Lord, in the spirit of humility and contrition of heart, and grant that the sacrifice which we offer this day in Thy sight may be pleasing to Thee, O Lord God.

lines.r: Raising his eyes towards heaven, extending and then joining his hands, the priest makes the Sign of the Cross over the host and the chalice, while he invokes the Holy Spirit.

lines.la: Veni, sanctificátor omnípotens ætérne Deus: et béne ✠ dic hoc sacrifícium, tuo sancto nómini præparátum.
lines.en: Come, O almighty and eternal God, the Sanctifier, and bless ✠ this Sacrifice, prepared for the glory of Thy holy Name.

sections.title: Incensing of the offerings
sections.about: At a sung Mass the priest incenses the bread and wine and the altar, saying part of Psalm 140. He is then incensed, and last of all the people: stand as the thurifer turns to you, and bow to him before and after.

lines.r: At a sung or solemn Mass the priest now blesses incense, saying the following prayers:

lines.la: Per intercessiónem beáti Michaélis Archángeli, stantis a dextris altáris incénsi, et ómnium electórum suórum, incénsum istud dignétur Dóminus bene ✠ dícere, et in odórem suavitátis accípere. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: May the Lord, by the intercession of blessed Michael the Archangel, who standeth at the right side of the altar of incense, and of all His Elect, vouchsafe to bless ✠ this incense and receive it as an odor of sweetness: through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.r: Taking the thurible, the priest incenses the bread and the wine, while he says:

lines.la: Incénsum istud a te benedíctum ascéndat ad te, Dómine: et descéndat super nos misericórdia tua.
lines.en: May this incense, which Thou hast blessed, O Lord, ascend to Thee, and may Thy mercy descend upon us.

lines.r: Then he incenses the altar, saying:

lines.la: Dirigátur, Dómine, orátio mea, sicut incénsum, in conspéctu tuo: elevátio mánuum meárum sacrifícium vespertínum. Pone, Dómine, custódiam ori meo, et óstium circumstántiæ lábiis meis: ut non declínet cor meum in verba malítiæ, ad excusándas excusatiónes in peccátis.
lines.en: Let my prayer, O Lord, be directed as incense in Thy sight: the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice. Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth, and a door round about my lips. May my heart not incline to evil words, to make excuses for sins.

lines.r: Giving the censer back, he says:

lines.la: Accéndat in nobis Dóminus ignem sui amóris, et flammam ætérnæ caritátis. Amen.
lines.en: May the Lord enkindle within us the fire of His love, and the flame of everlasting charity. Amen.

lines.r: The priest is then incensed, and after him the others in order, the people last.

sections.title: Washing of hands
sections.about: The priest washes his fingers at the side of the altar, saying part of Psalm 25, and returns to the middle to offer the sacrifice to the Holy Trinity.

lines.r: The priest washes his fingers to symbolize the great purity and inner cleanliness of those who offer or participate in this great Sacrifice.
Psalm 25:6-12

lines.la: Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine: Ut áudiam vocem laudis, et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua. Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ. Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam: In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus. Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: rédime me et miserére mei. Pes meus stetit in dirécto: in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
lines.en: I will wash my hands among the innocent: and I will compass Thine altar, O Lord, That I may hear the voice of praise: and tell of all Thy wondrous works. I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of Thy house and the place where Thy glory dwelleth. Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: nor my life with blood-thirsty men. In whose hands are iniquities, their right hand is filled with gifts. But I have walked in my innocence: redeem me, and have mercy on me. My foot hath stood in the direct way, in the churches I will bless Thee, O Lord.

lines.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

lines.r: Bowing down before the middle of the altar, the priest, with joined hands, says:

lines.la: Súscipe, sancta Trínitas, hanc oblatiónem, quam tibi offérimus ob memóriam passiónis, resurrectiónis, et ascensiónis Jesu Christi, Dómini nostri: et in honórem beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis, et beáti Joannis Baptistæ, et sanctórum Apostolórum Petri et Pauli, et istórum et ómnium Sanctórum: ut illis profíciat ad honórem, nobis autem ad salútem: et illi pro nobis intercédere dignéntur in cælis, quorum memóriam ágimus in terris. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: Receive, O holy Trinity, this oblation which we make to Thee, in memory of the Passion, Resurrection and Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in honor of Blessed Mary, ever Virgin, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, that it may avail unto their honor and our salvation, and may they vouchsafe to intercede for us in heaven, whose memory we celebrate on earth. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

sections.title: Orate, fratres and Secret
sections.about: The priest turns and asks the people to pray that the sacrifice be accepted; the server answers for all. He then says the Secret, the quiet prayer of the day over the offerings, and ends it aloud: “Per omnia saecula saeculorum.”

lines.r: The priest kisses the altar and, turning towards the people, extending, then joining his hands, says audibly:

lines.la: Oráte, fratres: ut meum ac vestrum sacrifícium acceptábile fiat apud Deum Patrem omnipoténtem.
lines.en: Brethren, pray that my Sacrifice and yours may be acceptable to God the Father almighty.

lines.r: The server answers:

lines.la: Suscípiat Dóminus sacrifícium de mánibus tuis ad laudem et glóriam nominis sui, ad utilitátem quoque nostram, totiúsque Ecclésiæ suæ sanctæ.
lines.en: May the Lord receive the Sacrifice from thy hands, to the praise and glory of His Name, to our benefit and that of all His holy Church.

lines.r: The priest answers in a low voice:

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: Then, with outstretched hands, he recites the Secret Prayers, not beginning with Oremus. The Secret Prayers vary with the Mass, and are found in the Mass of the Day.

lines.x: The Secret of the day is said here, quietly.

lines.r: He ends it aloud:

lines.la: Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
lines.en: World without end.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

sections.title: Preface and Sanctus
sections.about: The great prayer opens with a dialogue and the Preface, which changes with the season. At the Sanctus the bell rings three times: kneel.

lines.r: The priest begins the preface, a call to render thanks to God the Father, through Jesus Christ, in union with all the heavenly spirits. The prayer of thanksgiving and praise varies with important Feasts. The priest begins the Preface, holding his hands over the altar:

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.la: Sursum corda.
lines.en: Lift up your hearts.

lines.la: Habémus ad Dóminum.
lines.en: We have lifted them up to the Lord.

lines.la: Grátias agámus Dómino, Deo nostro.
lines.en: Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.

lines.la: Dignum et justum est.
lines.en: It is meet and just.

lines.x: The Preface is sung or said here. It changes with the season and the feast; two of the most used are given below.

prefaces.title: Preface of the Most Holy Trinity
prefaces.when: On Sundays that have no Preface of their own
prefaces.la: Vere dignum et justum est, æquum et salutáre, nos tibi semper et ubíque grátias ágere: Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus: Qui cum unigénito Fílio tuo et Spíritu Sancto unus es Deus, unus es Dóminus: non in uníus singularitáte persónæ, sed in uníus Trinitáte substántiæ. Quod enim de tua glória, revelánte te, crédimus, hoc de Fílio tuo, hoc de Spíritu Sancto sine differéntia discretiónis sentímus. Ut in confessióne veræ sempiternǽque Deitátis, et in persónis propríetas, et in esséntia únitas, et in majestáte adorétur æquálitas. Quam laudant Angeli atque Archángeli, Chérubim quoque ac Séraphim: qui non cessant clamáre cotídie, una voce dicéntes:
prefaces.en: It is truly meet and just, right and for our salvation, that we should at all times, and in all places, give thanks unto Thee, O holy Lord, Father almighty, everlasting God; Who, together with Thine only-begotten Son, and the Holy Ghost, art one God, one Lord: not in the oneness of a single Person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For what we believe by Thy revelation of Thy glory, the same do we believe of Thy Son, the same of the Holy Ghost, without difference or separation. So that in confessing the true and everlasting Godhead, distinction in persons, unity in essence, and equality in majesty may be adored. Which the Angels and Archangels, the Cherubim also and Seraphim do praise: who cease not daily to cry out, with one voice saying:

prefaces.title: Common Preface
prefaces.when: On weekdays and feasts with no Preface of their own
prefaces.la: Vere dignum et justum est, æquum et salutáre, nos tibi semper et ubíque grátias ágere: Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus: per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Per quem majestátem tuam laudant Angeli, adórant Dominatiónes, tremunt Potestátes. Cæli cælorúmque Virtútes ac beáta Séraphim sócia exsultatióne concélebrant. Cum quibus et nostras voces ut admítti jubeas, deprecámur, súpplici confessione dicéntes:
prefaces.en: It is truly meet and just, and profitable unto salvation, that we should at all times, and in all places, give thanks to Thee, O Holy Lord, Father Almighty, eternal God, through Christ, our Lord. Through whom the Angels praise Thy Majesty, the Dominions adore it, the Powers are in awe. Which the heavens and the hosts of heaven together with the blessed Seraphim joyfully do magnify. And do Thou command that it be permitted us to join with them in confessing Thee, while we say with lowly praise:

lines.la: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dóminus, Deus Sábaoth. Pleni sunt cæli et terra glória tua. Hosánna in excélsis. Benedíctus, qui venit in nómine Dómini. Hosánna in excélsis.
lines.en: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Sabaoth! Heaven and earth are full of Thy glory! Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is He that cometh in the Name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!

sections.title: The Canon: before the consecration
sections.about: The Canon is the unchanging heart of the Mass, and the priest says it in silence. He prays for the Church, the Pope and the bishop, and for the living (name your own here, at the Memento); he calls on the saints. When he spreads his hands over the offerings a bell rings once: the consecration is near.

lines.la: Te ígitur, clementíssime Pater, per Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum, Dóminum nostrum, súpplices rogámus, ac pétimus, uti accépta hábeas et benedícas, hæc ✠ dona, hæc ✠ múnera, hæc ✠ sancta sacrifícia illibáta, in primis, quæ tibi offérimus pro Ecclésia tua sancta cathólica: quam pacificáre, custodíre, adunáre et régere dignéris toto orbe terrárum: una cum fámulo tuo Papa nostro N. et Antístite nostro N. et ómnibus orthodóxis, atque cathólicæ et apostólicæ fídei cultóribus.
lines.en: We therefore, humbly pray and beseech Thee, most merciful Father, through Jesus Christ; Thy Son, our Lord, (He kisses the altar) that Thou wouldst vouchsafe to accept and bless (He joins his hands and signs the oblation thrice with the Sign of the Cross.) these ✠ gifts, these ✠ presents, these ✠ holy unspotted Sacrifices, (Then extending his hands, he proceeds:) which in the first place we offer Thee for Thy holy Catholic Church to which vouchsafe to grant peace, as also to preserve, unite, and govern it throughout the world, together with Thy servant N. our Pope, and N. our Bishop, and all orthodox believers and professors of the Catholic and Apostolic Faith.

lines.r: Commemoration of the Living

lines.la: Meménto, Dómine, famulórum famularúmque tuarum N. et N. et ómnium circumstántium, quorum tibi fides cógnita est et nota devótio, pro quibus tibi offérimus: vel qui tibi ófferunt hoc sacrifícium laudis, pro se suísque ómnibus: pro redemptióne animárum suárum, pro spe salútis et incolumitátis suæ: tibíque reddunt vota sua ætérno Deo, vivo et vero.
lines.en: Be mindful, O Lord, of Thy servants and handmaidens, N. and N. (The priest joins his hands and prays silently for those for whom he intends to pray. Then extending his hands, he proceeds:) and of all here present, whose faith and devotion are known unto Thee, for whom we offer, or who offer up to Thee, this sacrifice of praise for themselves, their families and friends, for the redemption of their souls, for the health and salvation they hope for; and who now pay their vows to Thee, the everlasting, living and true God.

lines.la: Communicántes, et memóriam venerántes, in primis gloriósæ semper Vírginis Maríæ, Genetrícis Dei et Dómini nostri Jesu Christi: sed et beáti Joseph, ejúsdem Vírginis Sponsi, et beatórum Apostolórum ac Mártyrum tuórum, Petri et Pauli, Andréæ, Jacóbi, Joánnis, Thomæ, Jacóbi, Philíppi, Bartholomǽi, Matthǽi, Simónis et Thaddǽi: Lini, Cleti, Cleméntis, Xysti, Cornélii, Cypriáni, Lauréntii, Chrysógoni, Joánnis et Pauli, Cosmæ et Damiáni: et ómnium Sanctórum tuórum; quorum méritis precibúsque concédas, ut in ómnibus protectiónis tuæ muniámur auxílio. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: We pray in union with and honor the memory, especially of the glorious ever Virgin Mary, mother of our God and Lord Jesus Christ: as also of the blessed Joseph, her Spouse, and of the blessed Apostles and Martyrs Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon, and Thaddeus; Linus, Cletus, Clement, Xystus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian, and of all Thy Saints, through whose merits and prayers, grant that we may in all things be defended by the help of Thy protection. (He joins his hands.) Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.r: Spreading his hands over the oblation, he says:

lines.la: Hanc ígitur oblatiónem servitútis nostræ, sed et cunctæ famíliæ tuæ, quǽsumus, Dómine, ut placátus accípias: diésque nostros in tua pace dispónas, atque ab ætérna damnatióne nos éripi, et in electórum tuórum júbeas grege numerári. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: We therefore beseech Thee, O Lord, graciously to accept this oblation of our service, as also of Thy whole family; and to dispose our days in Thy peace, preserve us from eternal damnation, and rank us in the number of Thine Elect. (He joins his hands.) Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.la: Quam oblatiónem tu, Deus, in ómnibus, quǽsumus, bene ✠ díctam, adscríp ✠ tam, ra ✠ tam, rationábilem, acceptabilémque fácere dignéris: ut nobis Cor ✠ pus, et San ✠ guis fiat dilectíssimi Fílii tui, Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
lines.en: Which oblation do Thou, O God, vouchsafe in all respects, (He signs thrice the oblation with the Sign of the Cross.) to bless, ✠ approve, ✠ ratify, ✠ make worthy and acceptable; (He signs again the Host and chalice with the Sign of the Cross.) that it may be made for us the Body ✠ and Blood ✠ of Thy most beloved Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

sections.title: The consecration
sections.about: The priest, bending over the altar, says the words of Christ over the bread, and then over the wine. He genuflects and lifts up the Host, and then the Chalice, for all to adore; the bell rings three times at each. Look up at the Host and at the Chalice, then bow your head. It is the custom to say silently “My Lord and my God.”

lines.la: Qui prídie quam paterétur, accépit panem in sanctas ac venerábiles manus suas, et elevátis óculis in cælum ad te Deum, Patrem suum omnipoténtem, tibi grátias agens, bene ✠ díxit, fregit, dedítque discípulis suis, dicens: Accípite, et manducáte ex hoc omnes.
lines.en: Who, the day before He suffered, (He takes the host.) took bread into His holy and venerable hands, (He raises his eyes to heaven.) and with His eyes lifted up towards heaven unto Thee, God, His almighty Father, giving thanks to Thee, (He signs the host with the Sign of the Cross) He blessed ✠ it, broke it and gave it to His disciples saying: Take and eat ye all of this,

lines.r: The words of the Consecration of the Host:

lines.la: HOC EST ENIM CORPUS MEUM.
lines.en: FOR THIS IS MY BODY.

lines.r: After pronouncing the words of the Consecration, the priest, kneeling, adores the Sacred Host; rising, he elevates It. -- Look up at the Sacred Host, with faith, piety, and love, saying: "My Lord and my God." -- and then placing It on the corporal, again adores It. After this he never disjoins his fingers and thumbs, except when he is to take the Host, until after the washing of his fingers.
Then, uncovering the chalice, the priest says:

lines.la: Símili modo postquam cenátum est, accípiens et hunc præclárum Cálicem in sanctas ac venerábiles manus suas: item tibi grátias agens, bene ✠ díxit, dedítque discípulis suis, dicens: Accípite, et bíbite ex eo omnes.
lines.en: In like manner, after He had supped, (He takes the chalice with both his hands.) taking also this excellent chalice into His holy and venerable hands (He takes the chalice in his left hand, and with his right he signs it with the Sign of the Cross.) He blessed ✠, and gave it to His disciples, saying: Take and drink ye all of this,

lines.r: The words of Consecration of the Chalice

lines.la: HIC EST ENIM CALIX SANGUINIS MEI, NOVI ET ÆTERNI TESTAMENTI: MYSTERIUM FIDEI: QUI PRO VOBIS ET PRO MULTIS EFFUNDETUR IN REMISSIONEM PECCATORUM.
lines.en: FOR THIS IS THE CHALICE OF MY BLOOD OF THE NEW AND ETERNAL TESTAMENT, THE MYSTERY OF FAITH; WHICH SHALL BE SHED FOR YOU AND FOR MANY UNTO THE REMISSION OF SINS.

lines.r: After the elevation of the Chalice, the priest says in a low voice:

lines.la: Hæc quotiescúmque fecéritis, in mei memóriam faciétis.
lines.en: As often as ye do these things, ye shall do them in remembrance of Me.

lines.r: The priest kneels and adores the Precious Blood; rising, he elevates the Chalice, and setting it down he covers it and adores it again.

sections.title: The Canon: after the consecration
sections.about: The priest offers the Victim to the Father, prays for the dead (name your own at the second Memento) and, striking his breast, for us sinners: the three words “Nobis quoque peccatoribus” are the only ones said aloud. The Canon ends as he lifts the Host and Chalice together and says aloud “Per omnia saecula saeculorum”; the Amen is ours.

lines.r: With his hands held apart, he then proceeds

lines.la: Unde et mémores, Dómine, nos servi tui, sed et plebs tua sancta, ejúsdem Christi Fílii tui, Dómini nostri, tam beátæ passiónis, nec non et ab ínferis resurrectiónis, sed et in cælos gloriósæ ascensiónis: offérimus præcláræ majestáti tuæ de tuis donis ac datis, Hóstiam ✠ puram, Hóstiam ✠ sanctam, Hóstiam ✠ immaculátam, Panem ✠ sanctum vitæ ætérnæ, et Cálicem ✠ salútis perpétuæ.
lines.en: Wherefore, O Lord, we Thy servants, as also Thy holy people, calling to mind the blessed Passion of the same Christ, Thy Son, our Lord, and also His Resurrection from the dead and His glorious Ascension into heaven: do offer unto Thy most excellent Majesty of Thine own gifts, bestowed upon us, (He joins his hands and signs thrice the Host and Chalice with the Sign of the Cross.) a pure ✠ Host, a holy ✠ Host, an unspotted ✠ Host, (He signs the Host and the Chalice, with the Sign of the Cross.) the holy ✠ Bread of eternal life, and the Chalice ✠ of everlasting salvation.

lines.r: Extending his hands, he proceeds

lines.la: Supra quæ propítio ac seréno vultu respícere dignéris: et accépta habére, sicúti accépta habére dignátus es múnera púeri tui justi Abel, et sacrifícium Patriárchæ nostri Abrahæ: et quod tibi óbtulit summus sacérdos tuus Melchísedech, sanctum sacrifícium, immaculátam hóstiam.
lines.en: Upon which vouchsafe to look with a propitious and serene countenance, and to accept them, as Thou wert graciously pleased to accept the gifts of Thy just servant Abel, and the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham, and that which Thy high priest Melchisedech offered to Thee, a holy sacrifice, an unspotted victim.

lines.r: Bowing down, with his hands joined and placed upon the altar, he says:

lines.la: Súpplices te rogámus, omnípotens Deus: jube hæc perférri per manus sancti Angeli tui in sublíme altáre tuum, in conspéctu divínæ majestátis tuæ: ut, quotquot ex hac altáris participatióne sacrosánctum Fílii tui Cor ✠ pus, et Sán ✠ guinem sumpsérimus, omni benedictióne cælésti et grátia repleámur. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: We most humbly beseech Thee, almighty God, command these offerings to be borne by the hands of Thy holy Angels to Thine altar on high, in the sight of Thy divine majesty, that as many (He kisses the altar.) as shall partake of the most holy (He joins his hands, and signs the Host and the Chalice with the Sign of the Cross.) Body ✠ and Blood ✠ of Thy Son (He signs himself with the Sign of the Cross.) at this altar, may be filled with every heavenly grace and blessing. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.r: Commemoration of the Dead

lines.la: Meménto étiam, Dómine, famulórum famularúmque tuárum N. et N., qui nos præcessérunt cum signo fídei, et dórmiunt in somno pacis. Ipsis, Dómine, et ómnibus in Christo quiescéntibus locum refrigérii, lucis, et pacis, ut indúlgeas, deprecámur. Per eúndem Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: Remember also, O Lord, Thy servants and handmaids N. and N., who are gone before us with the sign of faith, and rest in the sleep of peace. (He joins his hands and prays for such of the dead as he intends to pray for, then extending his hands he proceeds:) To these, O Lord, and to all that rest in Christ, grant, we beseech Thee, a place of refreshment, light, and peace; (He joins his hands, and bows his head:) Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.r: Pronounces in a somewhat elevated tone of voice, to symbolize an act of public self-humiliation; at the same time he strikes his breast in a token of contrition.

lines.la: Nobis quoque peccatóribus fámulis tuis, de multitúdine miseratiónum tuárum sperántibus, partem áliquam et societátem donáre dignéris, cum tuis sanctis Apóstolis et Martýribus: cum Joánne, Stéphano, Matthía, Bárnaba, Ignátio, Alexándro, Marcellíno, Petro, Felicitáte, Perpétua, Agatha, Lúcia, Agnéte, Cæcília, Anastásia, et ómnibus Sanctis tuis: intra quorum nos consórtium, non æstimátor mériti, sed véniæ, quǽsumus, largítor admítte. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum.
lines.en: To us also, Thy sinful servants, confiding in the multitude of Thy mercies, vouchsafe to grant some part and fellowship with Thy holy Apostles and Martyrs, with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicitas, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia, and with all Thy Saints, into whose company we beseech Thee to admit us, not weighing our merits, but pardoning our offenses. (He joins his hands.) Through Christ our Lord.

lines.la: Per quem hæc ómnia, Dómine, semper bona creas, sanctí ✠ ficas, viví ✠ ficas, bene ✠ dícis et præstas nobis.
lines.en: By Whom, O Lord, Thou dost ever create, (He signs thrice the Host and the Chalice, saying:) sanctify, ✠ quicken, ✠ bless, ✠ and give unto us all these good things.

lines.r: He uncovers the Chalice, and genuflects: then taking the Host in his right hand, and holding the Chalice in his left, he signs with the Sign of the Cross three times across the Chalice, saying:

lines.la: Per Ip ✠ sum, et cum Ip ✠ so, et in Ip ✠ so, est tibi Deo Patri ✠ omnipoténti, in unitáte Spíritus ✠ Sancti, omnis honor, et glória.
lines.en: By Him, ✠ and with Him, ✠ and in Him ✠ (He signs twice between the Chalice and his breast.) is to Thee, God the Father ✠ almighty, in the unity of the Holy ✠ Ghost, (He elevates a little the Chalice with the Host.) all honor and glory.

lines.r: Replacing the Host, and covering the Chalice, he kneels down, and rising again, he says (or sings):

lines.la: Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
lines.en: World without end.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

sections.title: Pater noster
sections.about: The priest says or sings the Lord’s Prayer alone, and the server or people answer with its last petition. He then prays to be delivered from all evils, breaks the Host over the Chalice and drops a small part into it.

lines.la: Orémus: Præcéptis salutáribus móniti, et divína institutióne formáti audémus dícere:
lines.en: Let us pray. Instructed by Thy saving precepts, and following Thy divine institution, we are bold to say:

lines.la: Pater noster, qui es in cælis. Sanctificétur nomen tuum. Advéniat regnum tuum. Fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidiánum da nobis hódie. Et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
lines.en: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy Name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation.

lines.la: Sed líbera nos a malo.
lines.en: But deliver us from evil.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: Then the priest takes the paten between the first and second finger and says:

lines.la: Líbera nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, ab ómnibus malis, prætéritis, præséntibus et futúris: et intercedénte beáta et gloriósa semper Vírgine Dei Genetríce María, cum beátis Apóstolis tuis Petro et Paulo, atque Andréa, et ómnibus Sanctis, da propítius pacem in diébus nostris: ut, ope misericórdiæ tuæ adjúti, et a peccáto simus semper líberi et ab omni perturbatióne secúri.
lines.en: Deliver us, we beseech Thee, O Lord, from all evils, past, present, and to come; and by the intercession of the Blessed and glorious ever Virgin Mary, Mother of God, and of the holy Apostles, Peter and Paul, and of Andrew, and of all the Saints, (He signs himself with the paten, and then kisses it.) mercifully grant peace in our days, that through the assistance of Thy mercy we may be always free from sin, and secure from all disturbance.

lines.r: He places the paten under the Host, uncovers the Chalice, and makes a genuflection; rising, he takes the Host and breaks It in the middle over the Chalice, saying:

lines.la: Per eúndem Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum.
lines.en: Through the same Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord.

lines.r: He puts the Part which is in his right hand upon the paten, and breaks a Particle from the other Part in his left hand, saying:

lines.la: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus.
lines.en: Who with Thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost liveth and reigneth God,

lines.r: He places the Half which is in his left hand on the paten, and holding the Particle which he broke off in his right hand, and the Chalice in his left, he says:

lines.la: Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
lines.en: World without end.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: The priest makes the Sign of the Cross with the Particle over the Chalice, saying:

lines.la: Pax Dómini sit semper vobíscum.
lines.en: The peace ✠ of the Lord be ✠ always with ✠ you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

sections.title: Agnus Dei
sections.about: The priest strikes his breast three times as he says the Agnus Dei, then prepares for Communion with three quiet prayers. At a sung Mass the choir sings the Agnus Dei; in some places the people stand until it ends.

lines.r: He puts the Particle into the Chalice, saying:

lines.la: Hæc commíxtio, et consecrátio Córporis et Sánguinis Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, fiat accipiéntibus nobis in vitam ætérnam. Amen.
lines.en: May this mixture and consecration of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be to us who receive it effectual unto eternal life. Amen.

lines.r: He covers the Chalice, genuflects and rises; then bowing down and striking his breast thrice, he says:

lines.la: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccáta mundi: miserére nobis.
lines.en: Lamb of God, who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.

lines.la: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccáta mundi: miserére nobis.
lines.en: Lamb of God, who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.

lines.la: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccáta mundi: dona nobis pacem.
lines.en: Lamb of God, who takest away the sins of the world, grant us peace.

lines.r: With his hands joined and resting on the altar, standing inclined, he says the three following prayers:

lines.la: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui dixísti Apóstolis tuis: Pacem relínquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis: ne respícias peccáta mea, sed fidem Ecclésiæ tuæ; eámque secúndum voluntátem tuam pacificáre et coadunáre dignéris: Qui vivis et regnas Deus per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: O Lord Jesus Christ, who saidst to Thine Apostles: Peace I leave you, My peace I give you: regard not my sins, but the faith of Thy Church; and vouchsafe to grant her that peace and unity which is agreeable to Thy will: Who livest and reignest God, world without end. Amen.

lines.la: Dómine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi, qui ex voluntáte Patris, cooperánte Spíritu Sancto, per mortem tuam mundum vivificásti: líbera me per hoc sacrosánctum Corpus et Sánguinem tuum ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis, et univérsis malis: et fac me tuis semper inhærére mandátis, et a te numquam separári permíttas: Qui cum eódem Deo Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas Deus in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who, according to the will of Thy Father, with the cooperation of the Holy Ghost, hast by Thy death given life to the world; deliver me by this Thy most sacred Body and Blood, from all my iniquities and from all evils; and make me always cleave to Thy commandments, and suffer me never to be separated from Thee, Who livest and reignest, with the same God the Father and the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.

lines.la: Percéptio Córporis tui, Dómine Jesu Christe, quod ego indígnus súmere præsúmo, non mihi provéniat in judícium et condemnatiónem: sed pro tua pietáte prosit mihi ad tutaméntum mentis et córporis, et ad medélam percipiéndam: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: Let not the partaking of Thy Body, O Lord, Jesus Christ, which I, though unworthy, presume to receive, turn to my judgment and condemnation; but let it, through Thy mercy, become a safeguard and remedy, both for soul and body; Who with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, livest and reignest God, world without end. Amen.

sections.title: Communion of the priest
sections.about: The priest says three times, striking his breast, “Domine, non sum dignus”; the bell rings each time. He receives the Host and then the Chalice.

lines.r: The priest genuflects, rises and says:

lines.la: Panem cæléstem accípiam, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
lines.en: I will take the Bread of heaven, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.

lines.r: Slightly inclining, he takes both halves of the Host between the thumb and forefinger of his left hand, and the paten between the same forefinger and the middle one; then striking his breast with his right hand, and raising his voice a little, he says three times devoutly and humbly:

lines.la: Dómine, non sum dignus, ut intres sub tectum meum: sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur ánima mea.
lines.en: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof; say but the word, and my soul shall be healed.

lines.la: Dómine, non sum dignus, ut intres sub tectum meum: sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur ánima mea.
lines.en: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof; say but the word, and my soul shall be healed.

lines.la: Dómine, non sum dignus, ut intres sub tectum meum: sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur ánima mea.
lines.en: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof; say but the word, and my soul shall be healed.

lines.r: Then with his right hand, making the Sign of the Cross with the Host over the paten, he says:

lines.la: Corpus Dómini nostri Jesu Christi custódiat ánimam meam in vitam ætérnam. Amen.
lines.en: The Body of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul unto life everlasting. Amen.

lines.r: He then reverently receives both halves of the Host, joins his hands, and meditates a short time.
Then he uncovers the Chalice, genuflects, collects whatever fragments may remain on the corporal, and purifies the paten over the Chalice, saying:

lines.la: Quid retríbuam Dómino pro ómnibus, quæ retríbuit mihi? Cálicem salutáris accípiam, et nomen Dómini invocábo. Laudans invocábo Dóminum, et ab inimícis meis salvus ero.
lines.en: What return shall I make to the Lord for all He has given to me? I will take the chalice of salvation, and call upon the Name of the Lord. Praising I will call upon the Lord, and I shall be saved from my enemies.

lines.r: The priest takes the Chalice and making the Sign of the Cross with it, says:

lines.la: Sanguis Dómini nostri Jesu Christi custódiat ánimam meam in vitam ætérnam. Amen.
lines.en: The Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul unto life everlasting. Amen.

lines.r: Then he receives all the Precious Blood, together with the Particle.

sections.title: Communion of the people
sections.about: The priest turns with the Host and says “Ecce Agnus Dei”, and then “Domine, non sum dignus” three times; say it quietly with him, striking your breast. Communion is received kneeling at the rail, on the tongue. The priest says the whole prayer, Amen included, so you do not answer. The same conditions apply as at any Mass: only Catholics who are not conscious of grave sin and who have kept the fast receive. If you are not receiving, stay in your place and make an act of spiritual communion.

lines.r: If Holy Communion is to be distributed, the server says the Confiteor. [This was omitted in the 1962 Missal.]

lines.la: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Joánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, ómnibus Sanctis, et tibi, pater: quia peccávi nimis cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ideo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Joánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, omnes Sanctos, et te, pater, oráre pro me ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.
lines.en: I confess to almighty God, to the blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the Saints, and to you, Father, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word, and deed, (Here he strikes his breast thrice.) through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech the blessed Mary, ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, all the Saints, and you, Father, to pray to the Lord our God for me.

lines.r: After which the priest communicates those who are to communicate, if there be any, saying:

lines.la: Misereátur vestri omnípotens Deus, et, dimíssis peccátis vestris, perdúcat vos ad vitam ætérnam.
lines.en: May almighty God have mercy upon you, forgive you your sins, and bring you unto life everlasting.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: Making the Sign of the Cross, he continues:

lines.la: Indulgéntiam, ✠ absolutiónem et remissiónem peccatórum vestrórum tríbuat vobis omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
lines.en: May the almighty and merciful Lord grant you pardon, ✠ absolution, and remission of your sins.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

lines.r: Elevating a particle of the Blessed Sacrament and turning towards the people, he says:

lines.la: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce, qui tollit peccáta mundi.
lines.en: Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him who taketh away the sins of the world.

lines.r: And then he says three times:

lines.la: Dómine, non sum dignus, ut intres sub tectum meum, sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur ánima mea.
lines.en: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof; say but the word, and my soul shall be healed.

lines.la: Dómine, non sum dignus, ut intres sub tectum meum, sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur ánima mea.
lines.en: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof; say but the word, and my soul shall be healed.

lines.la: Dómine, non sum dignus, ut intres sub tectum meum, sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur ánima mea.
lines.en: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof; say but the word, and my soul shall be healed.

lines.r: He administers the communion, saying to each:

lines.la: Corpus Dómini nostri Jesu Christi custódiat ánimam tuam in vitam ætérnam. Amen.
lines.en: The Body of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve thy soul unto life everlasting. Amen.

sections.note: The Confiteor before the people’s Communion is no longer in the Missal of 1962, but it is still said in many places.

sections.title: Ablutions and Communion verse
sections.about: The priest cleanses the chalice and his fingers, and reads the Communion verse of the day. Make your thanksgiving.

lines.r: The priest says silently:

lines.la: Quod ore súmpsimus, Dómine, pura mente capiámus: et de múnere temporáli fiat nobis remédium sempitérnum.
lines.en: Grant, O Lord, that what we have taken with our mouth, we may receive with a pure mind; and from a temporal gift may it become to us an eternal remedy.

lines.r: Then he holds out the Chalice to the server -- in Solemn Masses to the deacon -- who pours wine into it for the first ablution, then the priest proceeds:

lines.la: Corpus tuum, Dómine, quod sumpsi, et Sanguis, quem potávi, adhǽreat viscéribus meis: et præsta; ut in me non remáneat scélerum mácula, quem pura et sancta refecérunt sacraménta: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
lines.en: May Thy Body, O Lord, which I have received, and Thy Blood which I have drunk, cleave to my bowels; and grant that no stain of sin may remain in me, who have been fed with this pure and holy Sacrament; Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.

lines.r: The priest then washes his fingers and receives the second ablution. Then he covers the chalice and folding the corporal, places it on the chalice, as at the beginning of Mass, and goes to the right side of the altar to say the prayers from the Missal.

lines.x: The Communion verse of the day is read here.

sections.title: Postcommunion
sections.about: The prayer of the day after Communion, asking that the sacrament bear fruit in us.

lines.r: The priest kisses the altar. Then he turns to the people, and says or sings:

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.x: The Postcommunion of the day is said here. The server answers “Amen.”

sections.title: Dismissal and blessing
sections.about: The priest dismisses the people (stand for this at a sung Mass), bows over the altar for a last quiet prayer, and turns to bless them. Kneel for the blessing and make the sign of the cross.

lines.r: He turns to the people and says:

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.la: Ite, Missa est.
lines.en: Go, the Mass is ended.

lines.la: Deo grátias.
lines.en: Thanks be to God.

lines.la: Pláceat tibi, sancta Trínitas, obséquium servitútis meæ: et præsta; ut sacrifícium, quod óculis tuæ majestátis indígnus óbtuli, tibi sit acceptábile, mihíque et ómnibus, pro quibus illud óbtuli, sit, te miseránte, propitiábile. Per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
lines.en: May the performance of my homage be pleasing to Thee, O holy Trinity: and grant that the Sacrifice which I, though unworthy, have offered up in the sight of Thy Majesty, may be acceptable to Thee, and through Thy mercy, be a propitiation for me, and for all those for whom I have offered it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

lines.r: He kisses the altar, and raising his eyes, extending, raising and joining his hands, he bows down his head and says:

lines.la: Benedícat vos omnípotens Deus, Pater, et Fílius, ✠ et Spíritus Sanctus.
lines.en: May almighty God the Father, Son, ✠ and Holy Ghost, bless you.

lines.la: Amen.
lines.en: Amen.

sections.note: At a Mass for the dead the blessing is omitted.

sections.title: Last Gospel
sections.about: The opening of Saint John’s Gospel, read at the left-hand side of the altar. Genuflect with the priest at “Et Verbum caro factum est”, and the Word was made flesh.

lines.r: Then turning to the Gospel side of the altar, the priest says:

lines.la: Dóminus vobíscum.
lines.en: The Lord be with you.

lines.la: Et cum spíritu tuo.
lines.en: And with thy spirit.

lines.r: He then traces the Sign of the Cross, first upon the altar, and then upon his forehead, lips, and breast, and says:

lines.la: Inítium ✠ sancti Evangélii secúndum Joánnem.
lines.en: The beginning ✠ of the holy Gospel according to John.

lines.la: Glória tibi, Dómine.
lines.en: Glory be to Thee, O Lord.

lines.la: In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Hoc erat in princípio apud Deum. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt: et sine ipso factum est nihil, quod factum est: in ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hóminum: et lux in ténebris lucet, et ténebræ eam non comprehendérunt. Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Joánnes. Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine, ut omnes créderent per illum. Non erat ille lux, sed ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine. Erat lux vera, quæ illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. In mundo erat, et mundus per ipsum factus est, et mundus eum non cognóvit. In própria venit, et sui eum non recepérunt. Quotquot autem recepérunt eum, dedit eis potestátem fílios Dei fíeri, his, qui credunt in nómine ejus: qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis, neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt. Et Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam ejus, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre, plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
lines.en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by Him, and without Him was made nothing that was made: in Him was life, and the life was the Light of men; and the Light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to testify concerning the Light, that all might believe through Him. He was not the Light, but he was to testify concerning the Light. That was the true Light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world.
